rules.statement: A court has a duty under Section 70 to compel parties to bring a partition action to an end, and no party should suffer due to the court's delay.
rules.supporting_quote: 1. S. 70 states that no partition action shall abate by reason of non-prosecution, and it imposes a duty on the Court to 'compel the parties' to bring the action to an end - which duty the Court in this case has failed to fulfil. Where a delay in an action is the act or omission of the Court, no party shall suffer for it. 154 2. It is a rudiment of the law partaking of the character of a first principle that no party can lose rights by extinctive prescription nor acquire rights by acquisitive prescription after the date of the institution and during the currency or pendency of the action. 3. There is no legal impediment to the 4th defendant-respondent prosecuting the partition action in pursuance of s. 70 - any defendant in s. 70 means - any defendant irrespective of whether he has soil rights or not can prosecute the action thereunder. Quaere "Whether any action can be dismissed for want of prosecution after judgment is entered (as it is in this case).' LEAVE to

meta.parties: Peiris and Others v. Chandrasena and Others
